title: Pointers and Arrays
summary: An array's name turns into a pointer to its first element. Adding 1 to a pointer moves it by one element, not one byte, so p[i] is exactly *(p + i). Pointers can walk through arrays and strings, subtracting two pointers gives the distance between them, and a pointer just past the end is allowed as a stopping point.

cards.q: If p points at an int at address 1000, what address is p + 1?
cards.a:
1004

Pointer arithmetic moves by whole elements, and an int is 4 bytes.

cards.q: Which is the same as values[3]?
Two pointers into the same array, q - p, gives...
cards.a:
The number of elements between them

The difference is in elements, like the addition.

cards.q: Can a pointer point one past the end of an array?
cards.a:
Yes, as long as it is never dereferenced

It is the usual "end" marker for loops.
